speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have yellowing of the skin and eyes, along with some agitation; have you noticed any darkening of your urine or pale stools recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior, I need to rule out acute viral hepatitis, so I will check your liver function tests and viral serologies. Have you experienced any abdominal pain, nausea, or fever in the last few days?
REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests, Hepatitis_A_B_C_Serology

speaker: Doctor
text: Your liver function tests show significant impairment, but the negative viral hepatitis screen suggests another cause. Given your agitation and history of recreational drug use, have you experienced any muscle pain, weakness, or taken acetaminophen (Tylenol) recently?

speaker: Doctor
text: The mention of protection seems to be a transcription error or unrelated noise, so I will focus on your recent substance use. Have you taken any acetaminophen, herbal supplements, or potentially toxic mushrooms in the last two weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the severe liver injury with coagulopathy and the exclusion of viral hepatitis, I am concerned about acute liver failure from a toxic cause. Have you ingested any unknown mushrooms or herbal supplements recently, or did you take more than 4 grams of acetaminophen in the last week? REQUEST TEST: Acetaminophen_Level, Serum_Tox_Screen

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetaminophen_Level: Not detected. Serum_Tox_Screen: Positive for amphetamines and cocaine metabolites.

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive tox screen confirms recent stimulant use, which can cause rhabdomyolysis and acute liver injury, but we must rule out other causes of fulminant hepatic failure. Have you consumed any wild mushrooms, herbal supplements, or taken any other medications in the past two weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: The patient shows signs of psychomotor agitation and confusion. No other symptoms provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to assess the severity of your liver failure and check for other metabolic causes of agitation. REQUEST TEST: Ammonia_Level, Coagulation_Panel, CBC, CMP

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ammonia_Level: 180 μmol/L (elevated), Coagulation_Panel: PT 18 seconds (prolonged), INR 1.5 (elevated), CBC: Hemoglobin 16.3 g/dL, Leukocyte_Count 9,750/mm3, Platelet_Count 365,000/mm3, CMP: Bilirubin 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT 650 IU/L (elevated), TP_Activity < 40% (reduced)

speaker: Doctor
text: Your significantly elevated ammonia level explains the agitation and confusion, indicating hepatic encephalopathy. To pinpoint the cause of this acute liver failure, I need to see your abdominal imaging. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: The patient shows signs of psychomotor agitation and confusion. No other symptoms provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: With negative viral serologies, no acetaminophen toxicity, and a normal ultrasound, the severe acute liver failure with encephalopathy in a young male with stimulant use is most consistent with ischemic hepatitis or direct toxic injury from cocaine/ecstasy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Liver Failure secondary to Cocaine/Ecstasy Toxicity
